item.title: Astros Tender 6 Players Contracts, Re-sign 2, Non-Tender Trammell
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 30: Hunter Brown #58 of the Houston Astros reacts against the Chicago White Sox during the first inning in game two of the American League Wild Card Series at Daikin Park on September 30, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images HOUSTON, TX — The Houston Astros have tendered contracts to six of their arbitration-eligible players. Those players are RHP Ronel Blanco , RHP Hunter Brown , C Yainer Diaz , RHP Peter Lambert , SS Jeremy Peña and RHP Hayden Wesneski . Additionally, the Astros signed IF Nick Allen and LHP Bennett Sousa to one-year contracts for the 2027 season, and non-tendered OF Taylor Trammell . The announcements were made by Astros general manager Randy Flores . The deadline for Major League clubs to tender contracts to their arbitration-eligible players was today at 4 p.m. CT. Following today’s roster moves, the Astros have 38 players on their 40-man roster.

item.title: Coventry girls volleyball sweeps Hale-Ray for second straight Class S title and 14th overall
item.description: Coventry girls volleyball team celebrates their 3-0 win over Hale-Ray to capture the Class S volleyball state championship Friday, November 20, 2026 at Bulkeley High School in Hartford. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) HARTFORD - The Coventry High girls volleyball team has a lot of players who have state championship experience, be it on a volleyball or basketball court, a softball diamond, or a track. That experience helped the top-seeded Patriots on Friday against second-seeded Hale-Ray at Bulkeley High. Coventry swept Hale-Ray 3-0 to win a second straight Class S championship and the 14th in program history, all since 2003. Set scores were 25-17, 25-20, 25-19. Senior setter Teia Ransford, who had 36 assists, was named the most outstanding player. Coventry used the hitting of junior Hailey Mayo (15 kills), senior Tessa Young and others to take the state title. There was also the stellar defense of junior libero Aliza Sobol, who dug up a plethora of big hits from Hale-Ray. Coventry (23-3) and Hale-Ray (23-2) went back and forth early in the first set until Patriots senior Emma Weber stepped to the line. Six points later, the Patriots had an 11-5 lead. When a Mayo serve was not returned, Coventry took a 19-7 lead. Hale-Ray seniors Olivia Thiele and Fenway Jankowski each served an ace as the Noises attempted to claw back into the set. They got to within seven points on four separate occasions, but a Patriot block ended the set. The second set saw more back-and-forth play. The Patriots led most of the way, but never by more than four points until a Mayo kill made the score 20-15, and her tip two points later put the top seed ahead 21-16. Hale-Ray pulled within four points, 23-19, but a kill by junior Rowynn Myshrall got the lead to five again. Noises senior Reagan Bean smacked a kill to make it 24-20, but the second seed couldn't get the ball back over on the next point and the set ended. Hale-Ray never led by more than a single point in any of the three sets. In the third set, Coventry slowly built its lead out to four points, then five. Bean provided back-to-back points on a kill and a block for the Noises to get to within 17-14, then a Patriot hit into the net made it 17-15. From there, Coventry pulled away to claim its state championship. CLASS S GIRLS VOLLEYBALL STATE CHAMPIONSHIP Coventry 3, Hale-Ray 0 COVENTRY 25 25 25-3 HALE-RAY 17 20 19-0 Coventry highlights: Hailey Mayo 15 kills, Tessa Young 14 kills, Teia Ransford 36 assists. Records: C 23-3; H-R 23-2. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. Get the biggest headlines of the day from our network of journalists around the state. item.title: Dianna Russini working on a tell-all book after Mike Vrabel photo scandal: Boston sports radio host
item.description: Dianna Russini might be working on a tell-all book. On Friday, Boston sports personality Jim Murray claimed Russini is working on a book that will delve into the fallout from her alleged relationship with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel . “I have a little nugget for you,” Murray said on 98.5 The Sports Hub’s “Felger & Mazz” on Friday. “You remember Teddy Atlas, the boxing commentator? He has an annual event around Thanksgiving. It was held last night in New York, and she was there. A friend of mine was chatting with Dianna Russini, and she’s got a book coming out … She said she’ll be talking about everything that’s gone on, is what she told my friend.” According to 98.5 The Sports Hub's "Big" Jim Murray, Dianna Russini is telling people she has a tell-all book in the works. "She said she'll be talking about everything that's gone on, is what she told my friend." pic.twitter.com/wc6srhoXZt — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 20, 2026 “She’s come out with this podcast. It’s been one big nothing these last couple of weeks. Maybe [Vrabel] knows that a book is coming … She’s going to further expound on this whole situation.” Murray’s comments come just over a week after Russini returned to the sports media scene, launching her new show “The Russini Report” on BetUS TV, seven months after her departure from The Athletic amid the Vrabel controversy. Russini opened up on the “nightmare” photo scandal — first reported by Page Six in April — during an interview with People before her new show hit the airwaves. Dianna Russini during the debut of her new BetUS show, “The Russini Report,” on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. BET US “The best way to describe what the last six months were like for me is heartbreaking,” Russini said. “At the beginning of this, it was a nightmare.” She said she and her husband, Shake Shack executive Kevin Goldschmidt, deleted their X accounts after “lies” about the situation “became so out of control.” Russini has since returned to X and has posted about NFL news. “This was a runaway train, and there was nothing I could do to stop it,” she told People. “Once we realized nothing was going to stop this, it became unhealthy for us to read it because it wasn’t helping us heal. It was piling on and adding to what we were already dealing with.” Russini is also set to be a contributor on the “Nobody’s Safe” podcast with host Jon Weiner, who is popularly known as “Stugotz.” New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel speaks to the media after an NFL game against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images Her return to the spotlight comes as the Patriots’ season is falling apart. New England was blown out by the Lions in Germany to fall to 5-5 on Sunday. And it appears the Patriots will be without their star quarterback, Drake Maye, likely for the rest of the season after he fractured his fibula . item.title: Miami Heat GTA 6 Night Draws Record Fans And Massive Sales
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat and Rockstar Games turned a regular NBA matchup into a living version of Grand Theft Auto VI. Fans did not just watch a game on Wednesday night; they walked inside the world of Vice City. The arena in Miami became the setting for the game’s global launch, blending basketball with video game culture in a way few sports teams have attempted. The Wednesday night “A Night in Vice City” takeover featured a full arena makeover to celebrate the global midnight launch of Grand Theft Auto VI and attracted a surge of first-time ticket buyers. Hardwood floors and concession stands transformed into the game’s iconic locations. The team unveiled a special court design that served as the centerpiece for the night. Fans could buy food from fictional restaurants like Burger Shot and Cluckin’ Bell, which were set up in specific sections of the arena. The effort to make the whole building feel like the game paid off immediately. More than an hour before tip-off, local reporter Will Manso shared footage on X of unprecedented concourse crowds, admitting via Yahoo Sports UK that he had never witnessed such packed lines. A New Audience Steps In The most surprising result was the crowd makeup. Most people buying tickets had never been to a Heat game before. Per the same outlet, 95 percent of customers inside the team store were new shoppers, and overseas orders accounted for over 30 percent of all sales. This crossover brought in a group of fans who usually buy video games, not basketball tickets. The merchandise sold out fast, but some items remain available for those who missed the rush. Currently, five Vice-themed hats are listed as in stock on the Miami Heat team store website. Options for the Court Culture x New Era 9Fifty Snapback are available in “Vice City,” “Vice City Logo,” “Vice City Billiards,” and “Vice City Goodtime State,” and are priced at $50, according to Yahoo Sports. Giannis Shines in the Spotlight While the game theme drew the crowds, the on-court action delivered a dominant win. Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 27 points in his first game against his former team, the Milwaukee Bucks. He also grabbed 14 rebounds and dished out 9 assists. Hot Hot Hoops notes that in his minutes, Miami outscored Milwaukee by 12 points during a performance where he missed a triple-double by just one assist. Bam Adebayo added 26 points, and Davion Mitchell scored 24 on efficient shooting. The Heat used this win to extend their streak to six straight victories. With a 9-6 overall record, they have won 9 of their last 11 games and trail the second-seeded Boston Celtics in the Eastern Conference by just 2.0 games, per Hot Hot Hoops. The blowout allowed coach Erik Spoelstra to rest his starters early, limiting Giannis’s minutes in the fourth quarter. item.title: At 7-2, Have the Bears Met or Exceeded Your Preseason Expectations?
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Head Coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears walks out to the field prior to the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears have completed what Ben Johnson would refer to as “2 quarters” of the 2026 NFL season. Despite early adversity, they’ve managed to come away with only two losses so far – a mark that would be more impressive if they weren’t still sitting in 3rd place in their division. Still, the halfway point of the season presents us with a great opportunity to look back at the record predictions of a few of our WCG writers and evaluate just how close we each were to predicting this level of performance from the Bears. It also gives us a chance to look at our predictions for the remaining games and how confident we may now be feeling in those predictions. First, here’s the Bears’ remaining schedule: Week 11 – Nov. 22 vs. New Orleans Saints, noon on FOX Week 12 – Thanksgiving Day at Detroit Lions, noon on CBS Week 13 – Dec. 6 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars, noon on FOX Week 14 – Dec. 13 at Miami Dolphins, noon on CBS Week 15 – Dec. 19, Saturday at Buffalo Bills, 7:20 p.m. on CBS Week 16 – Christmas Day, Friday, Dec. 25 – vs. Green Bay Packers, noon on Netflix Week 17 – Jan. 3 vs. Detroit Lions, 3:25 p.m. on FOX Week 18 – Jan. 10 at Minnesota Vikings, TBD And here’s our look back… Donald Gooch: I had the Bears at 12-5 on the season, so if you project out their record over the next eight games based on the first nine, the expected record is between 11-6 and 12-5, so the Bears are on pace for what I expected before the season. I expect the Bears to meet, and perhaps exceed, my preseason prediction. Jacob Infante: My expectation was that the Bears would finish the year with a similar 11-6 record to what they had in 2025. Now, my expectations are higher, especially seeing their offensive improvement and after the addition of Jeffery Simmons to the defense. Their divisional schedule will be difficult to deal with, but my expectation is now that they’ll end the season with a 12-5 record. TJ Starman: My original prediction was for the Bears to end up 11-6. I was pretty accurate with my expectations for the first half of the season, though I did ultimately trade a predicted win in week 2 vs the Vikings for actual wins against both the Eagles and Seahawks. That said, I still expect 3 more losses in the next 8 games, which would put my adjusted prediction at 12-5. Josh Sunderbruch: I had the Bears at 10-6-1 and just barely making the playoffs in May, and I had guessed 6-3 at the bye, so they’ve beaten my expectations by one win so far. I can see them going 4-4 down the stretch, for 11-6, but I’d love for it to be 5-3 (for 12-5). Either way, I see them making the playoffs but losing out on hosting a home wildcard game due to a poor record against divisional foes.

item.title: Deadline acquisition Ray posts solid stretch with Friars
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 7: Robbie Ray #38 of the San Diego Padres walks off the field in the fifth inning during Game Four of the National League Division Series against the Milwaukee Brewers at Petco Park on October 7, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Matt Thomas/San Diego Padres/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Robbie Ray It’s never been easy to determine just what kind of pitcher Robbie Ray is. The veteran right-hander owns a 3.90 career ERA with 1,874 strikeouts across 1,606 2/3 innings. He won the AL Cy Young Award in 2021 with the Toronto Blue Jays, but posted a 3.71 ERA the following season. Ray has finished two seasons with a sub-3.00 ERA and seven seasons with a sub-4.00 ERA. But he’s never managed to achieve the kind of consistency that teams look for in reliable pitching. Overall Grade: C+ When the Padres traded for Ray at the 2026 Trade Deadline, he was in the midst of a career renaissance. In the final year of his five-year, $115 million contract, Ray posted a 3.08 ERA in 122 2/3 innings with the San Francisco Giant before being traded to San Diego. The Friars gave up shortstop prospect Joniel Hernandez and top pitching prospect Miguel Mendez in order to acquire the veteran. That’s a tough pill to swallow when considering that Ray is a 34-year-old rental. Ray was solid down the stretch, but immediately began struggling with command. His 5.08 ERA was mostly due to an insanely high 1.53 WHIP. Ray walked 27 batters in a mere 43 innings with San Diego. Still, he provided value and bolstered the Padres’ rotation down the stretch, pitching in three quality starts (nine total starts). Ray was also quite good in the postseason for San Diego. Walker Buehler was expected to start Game 1 against the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLDS. Instead, he was placed on the paternity list last minute and Ray took his place as the Game 1 starter. He started off quite well, and kept the Friars in the game, surrendering two runs over 2 2/3 innings of work.

item.title: Mets non-tender 3 players
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Mets non-tender 3 players appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the New York Mets look to sign players and make moves to bolster the team after a relatively disappointing 2026 season, there is no denying that some of the moves the ball club would make result from non-tendering players. While rumors surround the Mets and their pursuit of free agent star pitcher Tarik Skubal , the team has made moves to clean house a bit. According to MLB insider Mark Feinsand, New York is non-tendering such players as first baseman Christopher Morel, catcher Hayden Senger, and pitcher Dylan Ross. “The Mets have non-tendered Christopher Morel, Dylan Ross and Hayden Senger,” Feinsand wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Morel is the most experienced of the three, having been in MLB since 2022, and when it comes to the 2026 season, he spent time with the Miami Marlins and the Mets to close out the season. Playing in 36 games last season between the Marlins and Mets, Morel recorded a .173 batting average with one home run and six RBIs. There could be some fans thinking that the move to non-tender the three players is to make room for Skubal, though other teams have been doing the same and may not be linked to the star. Still, New York met with Skubal and left the meeting “impressed,” with MLB insider Jeff Passan saying Wednesday that the news reinforced “their status as favorites.” Regarding the deal the Mets would give Skubal, it’s projected to be a close-to-$400 million contract , which would make him the highest-paid pitcher of all time, if he were to accept it, via Jim Duquette. At any rate, it remains to be seen if New York ends up with Skubal and what further moves the team does make after finishing with a 74-88 record. item.title: Saint Mark's secures another state soccer title
item.description: FREDERICA – Saint Mark’s spent the first half repelling frequent St. Andrew’s scoring chances while getting a few of its own that the Spartans couldn’t quite finish. When Brayden Wrinn scored twice a minute apart early in the second half, the Spartans’ state title quest was just about done. They still needed some solid defense, which Wrinn’s teammates expertly provided. But those two goals help up in a 2-0 win over St. Andrew’s in the DIAA Boys Soccer Tournament final at DE Turf. “I actually thought first half, credit to St. Andrew’s, I thought they took it to us,” Saint Mark’s coach Dan Swasey said. “They had a great game plan. They wanted it. They were a little more physical than we were.” Wrinn’s 51 st -minute strike off Caleb Nelson’s feed on a counter-attack soothed Saint Mark’s worries. When he put the ball in the back of the net again one minute later, the Spartans could taste the title. “We didn’t really look great in the second half,” Wrinn said. “We knew we had to make a change because that’s all we have left in the season. “Caleb plays me a perfect ball. Just tap in. It’s great.” No. 3-seeded Saint Mark's (14-4) won its second straight Division II title and the 13 th state boys soccer championship in school history. Soccer split into two divisions in 2013. The Spartans won 11 state soccer titles during a 16-year span from 1986 through 2001. “First half our guys didn’t have it,” said goalie Thomas Swasey, the coach’s son, who also delivered several powerful free kicks to create offensive opportunities. “I gotta keep us in the game when our guys don’t have it. “I know they’re gonna score one or two and if I keep it to zero I know we’re gonna win because they’re gonna score one or two, every game.” No. 4-seeeded St. Andrew's (14-4) fell in the Division II title game for the third time in six years. The Saints won their lone state soccer title in 1981 and also reached the 1984 final. Saint Mark’s defense handled the challenge St. Andrew’s provided with Swasey fronted by center backs Declan Sullivan and Dylan Solomon. Senior central defender Brandon Kemp was out with an injury suffered in a quarterfinal win over Brandywine and Solomon stepped in. “We got to halftime. I think we made some adjustments that worked for us,” coach Swasey said. “I think our boys came out a little more juiced, a little bit more fire. “Once we got that goal I think it opened up and gave us a little more confidence that we could do it. We’re a little beat up and I think we just needed that confidence that we could make that goal and get them going so that was a big one by Brayden Wrinn.” Contact Kevin Tresolini at ktresolini@delawareonline.com and follow on Twitter @kevintresolini. Support local journalism by subscribing to delawareonline.com and our DE Game Day newsletter. item.title: Match Preview: BVB Face Last-Place Gladbach With Chance to Go On Top
item.description: DORTMUND, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 4: Konstantinos Karetsas of Borussia Dortmund celebrates his goal with Fabio Silva, Felix Nmecha of Borussia Dortmund during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Betis Balompie at BVB Stadion Dortmund on November 4, 2026 in Dortmund, Germany. (Photo by Vitalii Kliuiev/Getty Images) | Getty Images Borussia Dortmund have a chance to finish match-day 10 top of the table, and all they have to do is beat Borussia Mönchengladbach, the team that currently sits at the bottom of the Bundesliga table with an abysmal 1-1-7 record. If you don’t feel at least a smidgen of dread for tomorrow’s match after reading that statement, then you haven’t been a BVB fan for that long. Dortmund remain undefeated, but have drawn three of their last five league matches, so they could desperately use a win to start to build some momentum again. Meanwhile, Gladbach’s season has been a catastrophe, but their win and draw both came within the last three match-days, so there’s a chance they are starting to turn their season around. Player to Watch: Joe Scally In a season that has been shrouded in darkness, Scally has been pretty much the lone bright spot for Gladbach. The full-back/wing-back has three goals and two assists in nine matches for Die Fohlen, leading or tied for the lead in both categories. He’s fast, he presses very hard, and he is more than willing to bomb forward when the opportunity to present itself. I was able to watch Scally in-person when Gladbach visited Köln last month, and he stood out as the best player for the Foals by a wide margin. Predicted Lineup Prior to the break, the biggest question marks in the squad were Waldemar Anton and Serhou Guirassy, both with relatively minor muscle injuries. According to Ruhr Nachrichten , Anton should be set to return to the squad, but Guirassy still needs more time to recover. While he was unlikely to start anyway, the youngster Samuele Inacio has suffered a meniscus tear and will be out for several months. Fabio Silva has played well this season and in Serhou Guirassy’s absence, while Konstantinos Karetsas has been in good form and deserves to start. Meanwhile, the midfield trio of Joey Veerman, Felix Nmecha, and Jobe Bellingham has been excellent and needs to play. In the back four, I would be happy with either Ryerson or Gadou at right-back. Score Prediction Let’s keep the fun times rolling. I predict a 3-1 win for Dortmund with each of the front three: Karetsas, Silva, and Beier.

item.title: RSM Classic weather forecast: Heavy rain, 35-mph wind gusts expected Saturday
item.description: If the players thought wet, cold and windy conditions were tough on Friday at the PGA Tour's RSM Classic , they are bracing for worse during Saturday’s third round on St. Simons Island, Ga. This picturesque corner of southern corner of the Peach State –halfway between Savannah and Jacksonville – turned downright nasty on Friday. "Some of the toughest stretch of golf I’ve ever had to pay,” said Michael Thorbjornsen, one of three co-leaders at the midway point at 9-under 133, who played alongside Brooks Koepka and Blades Brown. “You’d pay money on every tee box for a par.” That bad, huh? “On hole 1, I think Brooks, Blades and I hit our drives around 240 (yards) straight into the wind. That kind of shows what it was like out there,” he said. “I don't think I've ever hit a drive that short in my life condition-wise.” More: PGA Tour player's brutal finish could cost him his card — and 10 others who missed RSM Classic cut Saturday’s forecast has the low-pressure strengthening as it moves northward along the coast leading to “higher confidence for areas of heavy rain and windy conditions“ Saturday morning, according to Tour weatherman Stewart Williams. The rain will become more scattered in nature Saturday afternoon as the system lifts to the north. If that isn’t bad enough, north to northeast winds of 15-20 gusting to 35 mph will decrease slowly during the afternoon as the system pulls away as well. Mostly cloudy skies and drier conditions return Sunday with highs in the upper 60s. The wind will be lighter averaging 10-15 mph. Players have become accustomed to unpleasant conditions for much of the FedEx Cup Fall schedule. Both the Butterfield Bermuda Championship, which was reduced to 54 holes, and the Austin Championship required a Monday finish. “Usually I kind of like it because some players don't like it,” said Adrian Dumont de Chassart. Added Rasmus Hojgaard: “No matter what golf course you play in conditions like this it's super tough.” This article originally appeared on Golfweek: RSM Classic weather forecast: Heavy rain, 35-mph wind gusts expected Saturday

item.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers Breaks Silence on Injury Ahead of Broncos Game
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders TE Brock Bowers. Getty The Las Vegas Raiders have been in a rut recently, losing six of their last seven games. A big reason for that has been a brutal schedule. Every loss has been against a team that is .500 or better. Unfortunately, things aren’t any easier this week, as the Raiders travel to Denver to face a 7-2 Broncos team. To make matters worse, the team’s best player is banged up. Tight end Brock Bowers had to leave the Week 10 game against the Seattle Seahawks due to an ankle injury. He avoided serious injury, but the Raiders listed him as questionable against the Broncos, which keeps the door open for him to play. Bowers hasn’t had a chance to address his injury status until now. He was vague about whether or not he’ll play against Denver. “I don’t know. We still have some conversations to have everywhere, so we’ll see,” Bowers said. He’ll likely travel with the team, but time will tell if he’s able to play. Pat Surtain Praises Bowers If Bowers plays, he should expect to be covered by Broncos star cornerback Pat Surtain. He’d normally follow a team’s top wide receiver, but the Raiders have a weak wide receiver room. Bowers is the biggest threat in the passing game, so Surtain will almost certainly follow him for most of the game. Surtain doesn’t think Bowers is a true tight end. “Some people think that he’s a tight end, I think he’s a receiver the way they utilize him in the route tree,” Surtain said, via Raiders.com . “I feel like his route tree and his yards per target is very telling. They utilize him in a multitude of ways that you have to be keyed in about. It’s all about honing in on the details and understanding how they’re trying to use him.” Surtain has seen many iterations of the Raiders’ offense and gave his thoughts on the current version. “It’s a different offense, like more of that West Coast offensive feel,” Surtain said. “They want to get started on the run game, and that leads to the play-action and stuff like that. It opens up their offense even more. They utilize a whole lot of personnel, 13, 12, 11, whatever how you look at it. It’s going to be a test for us just to get lined up in matching personnel.” Broncos Talk Fernando Mendoza The Broncos should be excited on defense, as they get to face quarterback Fernando Mendoza in his first road start. It’s going to be a tough day for the rookie, but defensive coordinator Vance Joseph likes what he’s seen from Mendoza thus far. “He’s got the great size, great arm talent, he’s athletic, he’s smart,” Joseph said. “He was poised, I mean did not look shook at all. The first half [against Seahawks] was really good, I think once [Brock] Bowers went out, it kind of hurt the game plan a little bit, but the first drive – I mean it’s 11 plays, touchdown. And he’s making plays with his legs. he’s making throws. … But he is poised, and he can make every single throw and it’s not too big for him.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Raiders TE Brock

item.title: Raiders owner Mark Davis 'hurt' by 'Madden' movie's portrayal of Al Davis | Exclusive
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis has “a million WTF moments in a day,” and the latest one is thanks to Prime Video’s “Madden,” he told USA TODAY Sports over the phone Friday in the aftermath of the film’s release. Davis said he was “hurt” by the depiction of his father, the late Al Davis – a Pro Football Hall of Fame executive and coach best known as the long-time owner, general manager and head coach of the Raiders. Although Christian Bale’s performance as Al Davis is being singled out by viewers and critics as one the film’s only silver linings film, which is largely centered on Hall of Famer John Madden , Davis wasn’t impressed. “It was full of turducken,” Davis said to USA TODAY Sports to describe the film in a nod to the Thanksgiving dish Madden famously popularized during his time as a broadcaster. “As far as representations of my dad, yeah, that hurts, and I did the best I could to protect him," Davis said. "It's absolutely a crime that they're able to treat people that have passed away and characterize them in ways that are unfair, and there's nobody around to protect their legacies. It's12 just unfair. I don't know what the purpose of the movie was to be real honest.” Before the film was released Nov. 18, Davis said the filmmakers reached out to him about certain aspects of the narrative. When he screened the final product two weeks before its release, Davis said he was shocked by a moment that hadn't previously been mentioned. The moment happens in the aftermath of the 1978 preseason game where Raiders safety Jack Tatum delivered a hit that paralyzed New England Patriots wide receiver Darryl Stingley. While Madden, played by Nicolas Cage, is devastated by the injury, Davis is depicted as dismissing Madden’s desires to go see Stingley in the hospital. “He’s not our player. We take care of ours, they take care of theirs. Okay?” Bale says to Cage, who is depicting a version of Madden who continues to worry despite being diagnosed with a bleeding ulcer. “You got such a big f– heart, but this is football, it’s not your job to take care of Stingley,” Bale says. “It’s your job to prepare for the next Raiders game. Do your job.” While the movie attempts to use the moment to highlight a philosophical clash between Madden’s empathy and Davis’ “just win” at all costs mentality, Davis said it disrespected his late father’s legacy. “One of the main legacies of my father was how much he took care of people, whether it was on the Raiders or other teams," Davis said. "People that were ill or needed help or whatever. He helped so many players on other teams that it's incredible. And he did it quietly. “And for them to put in the Darryl Stingley incident, that my dad was trying to talk John (Madden) out of going to see him – that was just such a hurt to me personally, because that's my father's legacy, is how he treated people. item.title: Tigers sign RHP Troy Melton to a six-year extension
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Troy Melton #52 of the Detroit Tigers delivers a pitch against the Chicago White Sox at Rate Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jayden Mack/Getty Images) | Getty Images While we were waiting for non-tender deadline news, and there was none involving the Tigers, who tendered contracts to all eligible players other than Matt Vierling, who was already DFA’d on Tuesday, the club had other business instead. They inked right-hander Troy Melton to a six-year contract extension that guarantees him $46.5 million with incentives and a club option for 2033 that could max out at $98 million over seven years. The hard-throwing right-hander will turn 26 years old in about two weeks. He has one year and 68 days of MLB service time currently, so this deal arrives as Melton was still five full seasons from free agency. Exchanging an extra year until free agency, and potentially two years if the Tigers use their club option, to guarantee himself at least $46.5 million is a pretty good deal for both sides. Melton wouldn’t have reached free agency until he was headed into his age 31 season, and with pitcher injuries being what they are, there’s always the risk that he wouldn’t be as valuable by that point in his career. From the Tigers’ perspective, they locked up six years of Melton at less than eight million a season, a bargain for a pitcher who is on track to be worth roughly 2 WAR per season if he continues on his current track. Of course, the Tigers, and no doubt Melton himself, expect continued improvements in the years ahead. With a 96-97 mph fastball with big extension that can reach triple digits, along with a deep and developing arsenal of pitches including a sinker, cutter, slider, curveball, and splitter, the potential here is pretty enormous. Melton just hasn’t found the strikeout touch consistently to take him into the upper tiers of starting pitchers around the league quite yet. 2026 was Melton’s first full season as a major leaguer after debuting in the second half of 2025 in a mixed role that included starts and high leverage relief appearances, and some good performances in the postseason. This season didn’t get off to a good start as Melton had some elbow inflammation in spring camp. The Tigers shut him down and took their time, getting him back on the mound in late May. Melton went on to make 20 starts totaling 114.1 innings pitched. He posted a 2.76 ERA and a 4.09 FIP over that span. He keeps balanced splits, leaning on that deep repertoire of pitches. With more consistency from his good slider-split combination, he should be able to strike out more hitters. For now, the fact that he attacks the zone aggressively and doesn’t issue many walks, while controlling contact, is a great foundation to build on going forward. item.title: Former Tigers Ace Tarik Skubal’s Offer Smashes MLB History
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - AUGUST 04: Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers celebrates a out a home plate by Tommy Edman #25 (not pictured) during the sixth inning against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field on August 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty Tarik Skubal has career news emerge. Getty The Detroit Tigers decided to trade ace pitcher Tarik Skubal in early August to the Los Angeles Dodgers after the Cy Young Award winner wouldn’t commit to signing a long-term extension with the club. While with the Dodgers, he helped them bring home another divisional title, but they were eliminated in surprising fashion by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series. Now an unrestricted free agent, Skubal is drawing interest from multiple clubs, but for now, it appears as though the New York Mets have the inside track to land him with what is being reported as the richest contract ever offered to a pitcher. Initial Offer For Former Detroit Tigers Ace Pitcher By Mets Revealed Getty Tarik Skubal has career news emerge. Per the latest report, the Mets are set to offer Skubal a contract worth nearly $400 million, which would break the records set by former Tigers Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer for the richest deals in MLB history for a pitcher. Via MLB Network’s Jim Duquette on X: “There has been a constant buzz since Vegas and multiple MLB sources have since confirmed that the initial Mets offer on Tarik Skubal was 9 years almost $400 million. That offer itself would far exceed the total dollars and would be the highest AAV for a free agent SP ever with likely other offers to follow. Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander $43.33M are the records currently.” Needless to say, this would be a tough offer for Skubal and his camp, led by power agent Scott Boras, to turn down. It’s already been revealed that the Dodgers aren’t likely to retain him since he allegedly prefers a longer-term deal, which they don’t want to offer. Mets President Of Baseball Operations David Stearns Implied He’s Open To A Long-Term Pitching Contract Recently, Stearns was asked if he had an aversion to signing pitchers to long-term contracts, to which he replied in the negative. “Every situation is unique,” the Mets’ president of baseball operations continued. “It’s been also well publicized even since I’ve been here, we’ve engaged in extremely long-term negotiations for pitchers, and we will do so again. But situation matters. The specific circumstance matters, and we do have to look at every individual pitcher on a case-by-case basis.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Former Tigers Ace Tarik Skubal’s Offer Smashes MLB History appeared first on HEAVY .

Just to be ourselves. Closing out the fourth quarter was a positive.” Castle then turned his attention to the Spurs offense. “Teams guard us differently and go from one through five, to blitzing, to packing the paint. Every team we play, it’s a different type of coverage. I don’t think it’s really a spacing thing for us. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.) item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
